newsitem.title: UK: HSBC turns to U.S. for telecoms.
newsitem.headline: HSBC turns to U.S. for telecoms.

text.p: Banking giant HSBC Holdings Plc on Tuesday signed up U.S. groups Unisys Corp and Hypercom Inc in a $50 million, five-year global agreement to supply a new telecommunications service to its 3,300 offices in 72 countries.

Unisys said in a statement released in London that it would also provide logistics, installation and maintenance services to support the rollout of Hypercom network technology to replace the former British Telecommunications network.
Over the five years, Hypercom would provide equipment valued at about $30 million and Unisys would provide services to a value of about $20 million, it added.
HSBC's current network, one of the largest private networks of its kind, provides financial products to it customers and is used to conduct its global business internally.
The U.S. companies will begin by replacing the 360 branch retail network operated by group members Hongkong Bank and Hang Seng Bank in Hong Kong.
This will be followed by networks in the U.S. for Marine Bank, in Canada for the Honkong Bank of Canada and the Middle East for the Saudi British Bank.
Unisys is a comprehensive services group that supports computing environments, whereas Arizona-based Hypercom provides advanced data communications technology to some 1,000 companies.
